## India: Regulatory & Legal Developments

IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has confirmed that the rules for the Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA) are now finalized and are expected to be published shortly. Concurrently, MeitY Secretary S. Krishnan indicated that there would be no extensions for DPDPA compliance deadlines, urging startups and businesses to prepare for implementation. ([Source](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMisAFBVV95cUxQakx6Y1RYS0lCdGEzN1VfZENmenhLRVZRWUViVUNwZHRCZzhZbDJFYkN4UUdOb1NKZzFKUHdIQnRxWDVINnhTaWY5Ml9IUFppTW44ZkVZeTFzTndwaUo2bl9GYmpHU3U4dkV5UEtGbHdXbG93OGs4QXBSQ3I5Ums5SDFGREdYRHdJQXp2YkpzcTVHaC0wLV9qaDlRRnp2Y25obXhIQVdjSHhsbjZFa0wwTA), [Source](https://news.google.))

The Supreme Court has sought a response from the Central government regarding several Public Interest Litigations (PILs) challenging the constitutionality of the DPDPA. This signals the start of legal scrutiny into the Act's foundational validity. ## India: Industry & Compliance Focus

WhatsApp is reportedly testing a new date-of-birth feature for users in India, a move seen as proactive preparation for the DPDPA's upcoming age-verification requirements concerning minors' data. This highlights how major platforms are adapting to the new privacy landscape.
